questions.q:
Last year I decided I wouldn't eat fast food for lunch any more.

Melanie goes jogging and answers her important emails before breakfast.

questions.rule: as well as answers. Notably, 'answering' shouldn't be used because 'goes answering' means she literally walks somewhere to answer these emails. The key phrase here is 'as well as'. questions.q:
My television needs fixing as soon as possible.

I must ___ as soon as possible

Clara says she doesn't usually go out at the weekend.

Clara says it ___ go out at the weekend.

questions.q: Then Coco Chanel returned from a ___ holiday with a tan and suddenly everyone else wanted one. (SAIL)

A sailing holiday is a holiday spent in the sea on a yacht or other similarly large sea vessel.

questions.q: Doctors' ___ changed too. (ADVISE)

questions.q: Better solutions came after an accidental discovery in the 1950s when a ___ found that a safe chemical, DHA, could be used in a lotion to fake a tan. (SCIENCE)

questions.q: Medical research also showed the ___ damage that sun can do to our skin and today fake tan is a much safer and more convenient alternative to sunbathing. (REVERSIBLE)

questions.q:

questions.q:
Richard hasn't believed in monsters for years.
KEY WORD: LONG
It's been ___ Richard believed in monsters.

questions.q:
That day was the first time that William realised his mistake.

William ___ his mistake before that day.
questions.rule: had/'d never realised. We have to use Past Perfect here to make it clear which event happened before the other. We use Past Perfect for the event that happened before the one we use in Past Simple. Past Perfect happens first, Past Simple takes place later.

questions.q:
Lucia thought that her brother's toys came alive at night.

Lucia believed that the toys ___ her brother came alive at night.

questions.q:
Francesca started telling stories before her brother was born.
KEY WORD: SINCE
Francesca ___ before her brother was born.
questions.rule: has been telling stories since. Use Present Perfect Continuous here, as we are bound by the keyword 'since'.

questions.q:
Luc was on a walk in the park when he saw something strange.
KEY WORD: THROUGH
Luc saw something strange while he ___ the park.
questions.rule: was walking through. We use a set of tenses to show that some shorter action took place during the longer action. He saw something (the short action) while he was having a walk (the longer action).

questions.q: Start by ___up with a good idea.
questions.rule: D - coming. 'To come up with something' means to think of something new, to invent something, to have a new idea. Another phrase from the list and a similar meaning is 'to think of something'.

questions.q: You can ___ out lists of ideas online to give you inspiration.

questions.q: Avoid places where you'll be ___ by people who turn and stare at the camera.

questions.q: Make sure there's nothing unusual in the ___ to distract from what the main actor's doing.

questions.q: It's an event which has been ___ place for centuries, and one which is attracting more and more tourists from around the world.

questions.q: It's an event which has been taking place for centuries, and one which ___ attracting more and more tourists from around the world.

questions.q: Whatever the reason, Jaipur's beauty is known ___. (NATIONAL)

questions.q: Tourists and artists are drawn from all over the world by the ___ of its colourful appearance. (ORIGINAL)

'What time did Sofia leave this morning?' asked Mack.

Mack wondered what time Sofia ___ that morning.

questions.q:

Marta ___ looking for the Northern Lights tonight.

questions.q:
'Please don't make a mistake when you book our flights' said Andy.

Andy asked Ben ___ when he booked their flights.

questions.q:

Natalia told me that ___ some fascinating activities that year.

Philip asked me ___ any memorable sunsets on my trip.

questions.q: As well as having around 50 assistants, Rodin ___ regularly invite friends, family and art lovers to visit his studio.

questions.q: Needless to ___, this is a place where artists such as myself can pay respects to the man we look up to.

questions.q: The act of regifting unwanted gifts is gaining in ___. (POPULAR)

questions.q: It keeps our homes tidy, saves waste and makes gift-giving more ___. (AFFORD)

questions.q: We should avoid passing anything on that was made especially for us, even if we find it ___. (APPEAL)

questions.q: Giving anyone the opportunity to discover their gift was unwanted is ___ and allowing it to happen is irresponsible. (SENSITIVE)

questions.q: Giving anyone the opportunity to discover their gift was unwanted is insensitive and allowing it to happen is ___. (RESPONSIBLE)

questions.q:
The outcome of the meeting was unexpected.
KEY WORD: TURN
The meeting didn't ___ we had expected.
questions.rule: turn out as / turn out how / turn out the way. To turn out means to have something as a result, e.g. "the party turned out to be a great success". Once again, you are given plenty of choice in phrasing your answer.

questions.q:
The price of petrol went up again a moment ago.
KEY WORD: JUST
The price of petrol ___ again.
questions.rule: has just gone up. The usage of Present Perfect is needed here to stress that the price increase happened at this very moment. The word 'just' usually implies the usage of a Perfect tense.

questions.q:
I was on a skiing trip in the Alps when I met Tom.
KEY WORD: WHILE
I met Tom ___ skiing in the Alps.
questions.rule: while I was. A combination of a continuous tense for a longer action ("was skiing") and a shorter action that took place during the long one ("I met Tom").

questions.q:
You must subscribe to use the music site.
KEY WORD: HAVE
You have ___ use the music site.
questions.rule: to have a subscription to. You might get confused by the two cases of 'have' here. One is a modal, with a meaning "need to", the other one is used in the more traditional sense of possession. The meaning here is that you need to have a subscription.

questions.q:
I often chatted to an invisible friend when I was a child.
KEY WORD: USED
I ___ an invisible friend when I was a child.
questions.rule: (often) used to chat to. We choose "used to" for repeated actions in the past that no longer take place.
